comparison: Both evaluate claims C12-C15 about virion arrest observations. OpenEval finds the experimental observations well-documented in videos and quantitative data. Peer reviewers requested clarification about the pre-arrested virion subset and arrest efficiency, indicating uncertainty about the interpretation and completeness of the data.

Both address gamma distribution fitting and kinetic interpretation (C16-C19, C46-C49). OpenEval finds the gamma distribution fitting appropriate and the 3-4 HA interpretation reasonable. Peer reviewers raised fundamental concerns about whether the proposed model could reproduce the observed distributions, requesting simulation validation because 'it is not intuitively clear' given the neighboring trimer requirement.

Both evaluate mutation studies showing fusion-peptide release is rate-limiting (C27-C35, C43-C45). OpenEval finds the data and inferences reasonable though notes alternative explanations not fully excluded. Peer reviewers explicitly affirmed this as a 'key insight' linking kinetic intermediates with structural requirements, stating it illustrates fusion-peptide release is rate-limiting for both arrest and hemifusion.

Both evaluate pH-dependent mutation effects (C36-C42). OpenEval finds the experimental data and mechanistic interpretation about carboxylate protonation reasonable and consistent. Peer reviewers did not question these findings, accepting them as part of the overall model linking fusion-peptide release to kinetics.

Both address simulation results (C50-C62). OpenEval finds the simulations appropriately test the mechanistic model with agreement between simulation and experiment supporting the model. Peer reviewers explicitly requested this simulation work to validate whether the proposed model could reproduce observed distributions, suggesting the results may not have been fully convincing without additional requested analysis.

Both evaluate the core mechanistic model of extended HA intermediate (C2, C82-C83, C89-C91, C126-C127). OpenEval finds the model well-supported by differential kinetics, mutation studies, and simulations. Peer reviewers affirmed this as the central finding and 'important contribution,' stating the work is consistent with an extended HA intermediate model that bridges membranes prior to hemifusion.

Both evaluate main conclusions about fusion-peptide release being rate-limiting (C2-C5). OpenEval finds these well-supported by kinetic experiments, mutation studies, and simulations. Peer reviewers explicitly affirmed this conclusion as a 'key insight' linking kinetic intermediates with structural requirements.

Both address prior work on cell-cell fusion and its relationship to current findings (C69-C71). OpenEval finds the citations appropriate and notes correct identification of limitations. Peer reviewers suggested investigating mutation effects on content mixing to test whether mutations affect the hemifusion to full fusion transition, indicating some uncertainty about how findings relate to complete fusion process.
